query: Which quantitative validation metrics and targets (confusion matrices, spatial overlap reduction %, acceptable error bounds) will demonstrate operational readiness to regulators?

response.query: Which quantitative validation metrics and targets (confusion matrices, spatial overlap reduction %, acceptable error bounds) will demonstrate operational readiness to regulators?
response.answer: For operational readiness, use confusion matrices, precision-recall curves, and acceptable error bounds for validation metrics. Aim for high accuracy, low false positives/negatives, and compliance with regulatory standards.

results.title: Capital Adequacy Requirements (CAR) (2026) – Chapter 3 – Operational Risk - Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions
results.content: For IRB credit risk approval, besides meeting the qualitative and quantitative requirements for an IRB rating system, institutions will need, at a minimum, to satisfy the following requirements to obtain approval with conditions (with a possibly higher initial floor): The institution is meeting the IRB use test principles.Footnote 10 The use test prohibits institutions from using default and loss estimates from their own internal ratings that are developed for the sole purpose of calculating regulatory capital, these systems must be used in other operations of the institution. [Basel Framework, MAR33.12] 9.6.4.2 Calculation of Capital Requirement for Modellable Risk Factors For those trading desks that are permitted to use the IMA, all risk factors that are deemed to be modellable must be included in the institution's internal, institution-wide ES model.
